title: Trust Boundary Standards — Private Deployment: mTLS, Export Contracts & Audit Schema
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the "trust boundary" standards we expect for Private deployments (VPC/VPN/on-prem) focusing on: mutual TLS expectations between control-plane and data-plane components, a compact audit log schema for SIEM export, an "export contract" (field-level mapping + retention guidance) for evidence automation, and a concise set of network segmentation and firewall rule templates.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers preparing customer onboards
- SRE/Platform teams implementing network templates for Private installs
- Security/compliance teams reviewing export schema and evidence retention

Summary of proposed approach (high level):
- Define three trust zones: PUBLIC-CLIENT, CONTROL-PLANE, DATA-PLANE.
- mTLS between CONTROL-PLANE and DATA-PLANE required; client certs for any inbound API from customer-managed networks.
- Minimum TLS: TLS1.3, ephemeral keys, certificates rotated every 90 days (shorter for high-risk customers).
- Audit log produce a canonical JSON line per request with an "export contract" mapping to SIEM fields.
- Evidence automation: a small set of periodically-produced artifacts (token-usage rolling windows, model-version rollouts, network connection graphs) packaged and signed for compliance reviews.

Trust zones (detailed):
- PUBLIC-CLIENT:
  - What: customer endpoints, external internet-facing agents.
  - Allowed interactions: HTTPS to CONTROL-PLANE API endpoints only. No direct access to DATA-PLANE GPUs/hosts.
  - Requirements: rate limit, WAF (optional), geo-blocking policy if requested.

- CONTROL-PLANE:
  - What: Redwood control components in customer private control plane (API gateway, auth, telemetry ingesters).
  - Allowed interactions: accept HTTPS from PUBLIC-CLIENT, mTLS to DATA-PLANE for management calls and rollout triggers.
  - Requirements: RBAC-v2 enforcement for management frames, audit emission at info/notice level for administrative actions.

- DATA-PLANE:
  - What: inference nodes, model stores, KV caches (in-cached memory store), edge proxies.
  - Allowed interactions: accept mTLS-only connections from CONTROL-PLANE; outbound egress to Redwood backing services only over dedicated peering or customer-approved routes.
  - Requirements: KV cache encryption at rest, local logging of token-level anonymized metrics, no control-plane credentials persisted in plaintext.

mTLS requirements and certificate lifecycle:
- Auth model: mutual TLS using X.509. Control plane uses CA managed by Redwood but stored in customer KMS for Private-on-prem installs when requested.
- Cipher suites: enforce TLS1.3 only; no RSA key exchange.
- Client certificate claims: CN must include component role (e.g., rp-controlplane-01), subjectAltName includes internal IP and service name.
- Certificate rotation: automated rotation via ops agent with a default 90-day TTL. Manual rotation must be supported via the console/CLI.
- Revocation: support OCSP stapling and a short-lived CRL published to the customer's monitoring endpoint.
- Handshake details: require TLS renegotiation disabled; require SNI match to expected service name.

Firewall and segmentation patterns (templates):
- Principle: minimal attack surface; default-deny; explicit allow lists.
- Example template (CIDR placeholders):
  - CONTROL-PLANE-TO-DATA-PLANE: allow TCP 443 only from CONTROL-PLANE-CIDR to DATA-PLANE-CIDR (mTLS port).
  - DATA-PLANE-OUTBOUND: allow TCP 443 to REDWOOD_BACKEND_CIDR for metrics and model pulls, deny otherwise.
  - MANAGEMENT-INGRESS: allow SSH/RDP only from customer-admin CIDR via jumpbox; log and alert any attempt from other CIDRs.
  - KV-STORE: allow internal ports (e.g., 6379) only within DATA-PLANE-CIDR and from authorized proxy nodes.

Firewall rule examples (pseudo-iptables / cloud rule):
- deny all inbound
- allow proto tcp from 10.10.0.0/24 to 10.20.0.0/24 port 443 comment "control->data mTLS"
- allow proto tcp from 10.20.0.0/24 to 198.51.100.0/24 port 443 comment "data->redwood backend"

RBAC-v2 mapping notes (brief):
- Roles: viewer, operator, deployer, admin. Entities: human users, service principals (control-plane agents), customer-integrations.
- Policy files should be JSON or Rego; recommended attributes: principal_id, role, scope (project, cluster, model), conditions (timewindow, ip_range).
- Enforcement point: API gateway and control-plane components; decisions logged as part of audit event (see schema below).

Audit log schema (canonical JSON-line format):
- We propose a compact but expressive schema to make SIEM mapping simple. Each event is a single line JSON with the following keys (field explanations after):
  - ts, event_id, level, actor, actor_type, action, target, target_type, req_id, svc_component, src_ip, dst_ip, auth_method, rbac_role, outcome, details, sha256_artifact, retention_tier

Field explanations and example values:
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (e.g., 2024-10-22T14:02:12Z)
- event_id: UUIDv4 for the event
- level: debug|info|notice|warning|error|critical
- actor: "u:alice@acme.com" or "svc:rp-controller-01"
- actor_type: human|service|external
- action: e.g., model.deploy, rollout.trigger, token.generate, config.update
- target: resource identifier (e.g., model:openllama-7b-v1)
- target_type: model|node|config|network
- req_id: correlation id propagated across RPCs
- svc_component: logical component name (control-plane-auth, dataplane-proxy, telemetry-ingest)
- src_ip, dst_ip: IPv4/6 or empty if not applicable
- auth_method: oauth|mTLS|api_key|none
- rbac_role: role used in decision (e.g., deployer)
- outcome: success|denied|error|partial
- details: free-form short message (<= 1024 chars)
- sha256_artifact: optional, sha256 of artifact attached to event (evidence file)
- retention_tier: hot|warm|cold (used for evidence automation export)

Examples (one-line JSON):
{"ts":"2024-10-22T14:02:12Z","event_id":"a3f9e1c4-5c0a-4b2e-9e1f-9f8d2c1b7a3e","level":"notice","actor":"svc:rp-controller-01","actor_type":"service","action":"rollout.trigger","target":"model:openllama-7b-v1","target_type":"model","req_id":"req-9a8b7c","svc_component":"control-plane-orchestrator","src_ip":"10.10.0.5","dst_ip":"10.20.0.12","auth_method":"mTLS","rbac_role":"deployer","outcome":"success","details":"canary rollout started to pool-a","sha256_artifact":"","retention_tier":"hot"}

SIEM export contract (mapping to common SIEM fields):
- ecs.timestamp -> ts
- ecs.event.id -> event_id
- ecs.event.outcome -> outcome
- user.name -> actor (strip svc: prefix for humans)
- source.ip -> src_ip
- destination.ip -> dst_ip
- process.name -> svc_component
- network.direction -> infer from src_ip/dst_ip and zone mapping
- event.module -> derived from svc_component prefix mapping
Notes: export pipeline should tag each event with customer_id and region fields (not shown above) when exporting to shared SIEM.

Evidence automation and "export contract" details:
- Periodic artifacts to produce per customer (default cadence weekly, escalated to daily for high-risk):
  - signed-audit-bundle.jsonl.gz: gzipped newline-delimited JSON with the canonical schema above plus a signed manifest and bundle signature.
  - connection-graph-YYYYMMDD.dot: Graphviz dot file depicting last-week connection attempts (edges: src->dst annotated with port/protocol and count).
  - rbac-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.json: list of active RBAC policies mapped to entities.
  - cert-rotation-log-YYYYMMDD.csv: rotation events for mTLS certs.

- Packaging & signing:
  - Each artifact MUST include a manifest.json with sha256 of artifacts, creation_ts, and signer identity.
  - Signer: ops-agent signs with a key that can be validated via customer's KMS public key when requested.

- Retention & tiers:
  - hot: 90 days by default (detailed events)
  - warm: 1 year for aggregated summaries
  - cold: 7 years for compliance-sensitive customers (requires explicit contract)

Runbook (quick):
- On suspicious network activity (SIG):
  1) Pull last 24h signed-audit-bundle and connection-graph.
  2) Validate manifest signature using ops-agent public key.
  3) Correlate req_id across control-plane and data-plane logs.
  4) If lateral movement suspected, trigger temporary deny-list at firewall and escalate to security@redwood.ai.

- On failed mTLS handshake storms:
  1) Check cert-rotation-log for mass expirations.
  2) Verify system clock drift on nodes (NTP).
  3) If CA compromised/suspected, rotate and publish CRL/OCSP update; prepare signed evidence bundle for audit.

Diagram (ASCII quick reference):
  PUBLIC-CLIENT ---> CONTROL-PLANE (HTTPS, auth) 
                       |
                       | mTLS (443)
                       v
                    DATA-PLANE (mTLS only)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default certificate TTL for high-security tenants (90d vs 30d).
- Should we mandate HSM-backed key generation for every Private customer or only enterprise tier?
- Define exact retention SLAs for evidence exports in the contract templates.

Notes to self / implementation hints:
- Keep audit schema compact to avoid high egress costs for high-throughput customers. Use "retention_tier" to gate what fields are emitted in hot vs warm exports.
- For SIEM mapping, provide a small adapter library (python/node) that maps our keys to ECS fields; include field-level masking helpers.
- Consider adding sequence numbers to events for easier reassembly in SIEM when log shipping is lossy.

Appendix: quick checklist before handoff to customer ops (short):
- [ ] Confirm CONTROL-PLANE and DATA-PLANE CIDRs
- [ ] Verify KMS access or arrange HSM key provisioning
- [ ] Confirm cert TTL and rotation window
- [ ] Enable signed-audit-bundle export and provide SIEM endpoint details
- [ ] Apply baseline firewall templates and run internal network scan

End of doc.
